scope_statement: Radiological appearance of the distal femur.
source_note: No sources were retrieved. The generation environment had no access to PubMed, Cochrane, any journal or any textbook. The Tier 1 source minimum is NOT met and this draft would not pass Tier 1 in the deployed pipeline. This is the first section on the site written entirely for professionals, and it is unverified.
claims_needing_verification: Vessel position, physeal scar level and epicondylar to posterior condylar rotation all vary and are all visible preoperatively.
Rotational assessment is the imaging question with the most direct surgical consequence.
Tunnel and hardware position relative to native attachments decides single versus two stage revision.
Where imaging and textbook disagree, the patient's anatomy wins.
claims_note: Listed above are the substantive claims, taken from the deepest tier's key learning points. Every anatomical statement in the page body requires the same verification against a standard text; these are the ones a reviewer should start with.
content_rule: Decision 005: this page carries no measurement, angle, dimension, distance, normal range or incidence figure, because none could be verified. Every published description of this anatomy is quantitative, so the absence is visible and deliberate. A reviewer with sources should add the figures with a date against each one rather than treat their absence as an oversight.
gaps_or_uncertainties: No measurement, angle, dimension or normal range appears anywhere on this page.
Anatomical relations are described in relative terms, which is adequate for orientation and inadequate for planning that depends on a dimension.
